newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA Peugeot details Jan performance.
newsitem.headline: PSA Peugeot details Jan performance.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen registered the biggest sales drop in January of any European carmaker, but the French company said on Thursday that the 12.3 percent drop in its European car sales was due to the fall in the French market.
It said in a statement that its sales in Europe excluding France rose 6.6 percent in volume terms and it gained market share in Spain, Italy, Britain and the Benelux countries.
The Brussels-based European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA) reported on Thursday that European car sales fell 2.9 percent in January, and the Peugeot group's sales fell 12.3 percent.

"The European market in January 1997 showed sharply contrasting performances in France and the rest of Europe -- the French market fell 33.7 percent, while the European market excluding France was up 2.5 percent," the PSA statement said.

"In the European market excluding France, PSA Peugeot Citroen increased its car registrations in volume terms by 6.6 percent. The group thus registered the second biggest gain among the mass producers. PSA Peugeot Citroen had 9.1 percent of the European market excluding France in January 1997, compared with 8.7 percent in January 1996," it said.

Its share of the European market, France included, fell to 10.7 percent in January from 11.8 percent, leaving it in fifth place behind leader Volkswagen, Fiat, General Motors and Ford, but ahead of the smallest of Europe's Big Six, Renault.

Renault's car sales in Europe fell 6.4 percent in January, reflecting its stronger performance in its home market. In France, the PSA group's car sales fell 43 percent while Renault sales were down 29.3 percent. The PSA group said the reason its sales were off so sharply was that it lagged other carmakers in offering promotions and discounts to protect its profit margins.
